credit.zh: 四座地标均为程序化建模，glTF 2.0 实时渲染
credit.en: All four landmarks are procedurally modelled and rendered live from glTF 2.0

blurb.zh: 为 1889 年巴黎世博会而建，1.8 万余个铁构件铆成 300 米高的镂空格构。它曾被巴黎文艺界联名反对，如今却是这座城市最无可替代的剪影。
blurb.en: Built for the 1889 Exposition Universelle, its 18,000 iron parts rivet into a 300-metre open lattice. Parisian artists once petitioned against it; today it is the city's most irreplaceable silhouette.

blurb.zh: 不是一堵墙，而是一整套横跨山脊的防御体系：墙体顺着地势起伏，敌楼与烽燧在隘口相望。今天看到的大部分砖石长城，是明代陆续修筑的。
blurb.en: Not one wall but a defence system strung across ridgelines: rammed walls follow the terrain while watchtowers and beacon fires answer each other at the passes. Most brick-and-stone sections visible today were built under the Ming.

blurb.zh: 明清两代的皇权中心，980 座建筑沿一条中轴线层层展开。黄琉璃瓦压着朱红宫墙，太和殿的台基把整座城市抬高一截。
blurb.en: The imperial seat of the Ming and Qing for five centuries: 980 buildings unfolding along a single axis, yellow glazed tiles over vermilion walls, the Hall of Supreme Harmony lifted on its own terrace.

blurb.zh: 沙贾汗为亡妻穆塔兹·马哈尔所建的白色大理石陵墓。四座宣礼塔微微向外倾斜，据说是为了在地震时倒向远离主墓的方向。
blurb.en: Shah Jahan's white-marble mausoleum for Mumtaz Mahal. The four minarets lean slightly outward — so the story goes, so that an earthquake would topple them away from the tomb.
